_comment_scope: A CURATED SUBSET, deliberately: only the tests that can kill mutants in the
modules below, because `coverageAnalysis: off` makes every mutant re-run the
whole command. That design has one failure mode, and Miguel hit it on PR #42:
a module added to `mutate` whose tests were never added to the command scores
against a suite that cannot see it, and the report does not say so.
So the rule when touching either list: a file in `mutate` must have its tests
in `command`, and adding a test file here is how a new module earns its place.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT: test/renderer-scope.test.js and the repo-scanning tests.
Their subject is the REPOSITORY rather than a function -- the shared-scope
allow-list fails on Stryker's own instrumentation globals, and the
git-ls-files and control-character guards assert about the file tree, which
Stryker's sandbox is a copy of. They kill no mutant, because nothing they
assert is an expression a mutator can reach.
(PR 1b). They race REAL processes for a lock -- seconds each, re-run for every
mutant -- and the mutants they catch (unlink by path, no .break, an unbound
async verdict) also die in lock-breaker.test.js and session-lock.test.js,
which ARE here. They require nothing from host/ themselves (the children do),
so test/stryker-config.test.js doesn't ask for them.
_comment_resources: #63's Resources modules (host/resource-*.js, host/chip-store.js, app/resources-*.js) are all here: they decide what
Stop kills, so a wrong verdict ends somebody's process (test/stryker-config.test.js pins that they stay).
None is skipped. host/resource-kill.js and host/resource-sampler.js hold PowerShell, but each also holds JS logic
(target validation, result parsing, the script text) that the fast tests pin.
REAL-PROCESS TESTS ARE SKIPPED BY NAME, not by file: the command's --test-skip-pattern drops the tests that spawn real
PowerShell (seconds each, re-run for every mutant) while resource-stop-position.test.js and resource-stop-respawn.test.js
stay, because their fast tests (the kill script's text, the extras report, the tree/position rules) are what kill the
script mutants. test/stryker-config.test.js names those tests (REAL_PROCESS_TESTS), proves the pattern matches each of
them and nothing else, and proves each still spawns real processes, so the exemption can only shrink.
--test-concurrency=2 caps the node test runner inside every mutant run (CPU budget).
THE PATTERN'S RULE: --test-skip-pattern is an UNANCHORED SUBSTRING regex tested against the TITLE of every test in the
WHOLE command, not just the resource files. Any title anywhere containing one of its alternatives is skipped, so a new
title that merely mentions 'real PowerShell' would vanish from the run. The config test fails if the pattern matches a
title outside the three named files, and if a test that spawns a real process (decided by what it does) is not matched.
FOR MORTIMER (timeouts): the node test runner is capped at 2 per mutant run, so a mutant run is slower than the plain
suite; timeoutMS (60 s) is the ceiling and STRYKER SCORES A TIMEOUT AS KILLED, so read the timeout count in the report.
FOR MORTIMER (survivors by design): the PowerShell script bodies in host/resource-kill.js and host/resource-sampler.js are
strings only the skipped real-process tests can really execute; script-text mutants that no fast test pins will survive
by design. Judge those as accepted survivors, not as missing tests.
_comment_rule_is_enforced: THE RULE ABOVE IS NOW A TEST, because I broke it by hand twice in the two
commits immediately after writing it. Mortimer found six test files that
exercise mutated modules and were absent from `command` -- including the two
newest, which are where H1-H5 and I1 are tested, so the most recently changed
code on the branch was being measured against a suite that could not see its
tests. Those kills existed; Stryker was never told to run them.
A rule written in a comment is a rule nothing enforces. See
test/stryker-config.test.js: every module in `mutate` must have every test
file that requires it present in `command`, derived by reading the requires
rather than by restating the list.

_comment_timeout: RAISED from 20000 for PR #42. app/secret-vault.js now derives keys with
scrypt at N=2^17, ~200ms per derivation by design, and STRYKER COUNTS A
TIMEOUT AS KILLED -- so a timeout is a PHANTOM KILL, the exact mirror of the
phantom survivor, and a comfortable score can be made of clocks rather than
assertions. Miguel raised this before the run rather than after.
Two mitigations, both applied: the lock suites inject cheap parameters
(N=1024) and a short file-lock deadline, so only the handful of tests that
deliberately exercise the REAL cost pay it; and the ceiling is high enough
that a mutant slowing a derivation still finishes and is judged on assertions.
READ THE TIMEOUT COUNT IN THE REPORT, not only the score.
